page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text, with a short italic verse couplet set below the paragraphs; no marginal notes. Page number at the head right. Catchword "Sequi-" at the foot right, signature "Ii 4" at the foot.

main_text.l: 7. Dextra pars mundi Geographis dicitur o-
rientalis, Siniftra vero occidentalis: nonnullis
vero dextra pars dicitur Meridies, Siniftra, Se-
ptentrio.
Dextrum & finiftrum in cœlo & terra relatiue dici-
tur respectu manus dextræ ac finiftræ in homine: nam
si faciem homo vertat versus aliquam cœli plagam,
neceffariæ ei vna plaga ad dextram erit, altera ad fi-
niftram, tertia versus ipfam faciem, quarta à tergo. Ita-
que cum aliam cœli plagam respiciant alii artifices pro
diuerso fuo fcopo, fit vt hæc aliis, aliis illa cœli pars
Dextra aut Siniftra vocetur: nam Poetæ propter in-
fulas Fortunatas faciem vertunt ad occasum, ideo Poe-
tis plaga feptentrionalis eft dextra, meridionalis finiftra.
Aftronomi faciem vertunt versus meridiem, ideo
illis plaga occidentalis eft dextra, orientalis finiftra.
Geographi nonnulli dicunt fe faciem vertere ad fe-
ptentr. propter polum articticum, ideo illis orientalis
pars mundi eft dextra, occidentalis finiftra. Sacerdotes
faciem vertunt ad ortum, quod & augures olim faci-
ebant, ideo illis meridies eft ad dextram feptentrio ad
finiftram secundum vfitatos versus.

l.i: Ad boream terra, fed cœli menfor ad auftrum,
Prato Dei exortum videt, occasumq; Poeta.

main_text.l: Intermediæ plagæ funt, quæ à cardinalibus
plagis declinant, fiue quæ mediæ funt inter car-
dinales plagas, nempe inter ortum & meridiem,
inter ortum & fept. inter occasum & merid. in-
ter occasum & fept. vel contra inter fept. & ortū,
inter fept. & occasum, inter merid. & ortum, in-
ter meridiem & occasum.
De his theorema eft: Geographi 12. plagas in-
termedias, nautæ vero 28. constituunt, quas pla-
gas diuerfis ventorum nominib. infigniunt, vt in
compaffo nautico ad oculum videre licet.

page.notes: Printed in an old typeface; the "I" of "Ii 4" is the gathering signature. The couplet is set in italic. Some words are uncertain in the scan, notably "fit vt" and "Sacerdotes" which are read as printed. The page is shown with a dark binding edge and show-through at the right, which are not transcribed.
